**The big one.** Everything since v0.7.4: a whole climate, weather that
moves and gets moved, a new episode, Phobos in the main build, tunnels that
sound like tunnels, and a long list of smaller things. As always, nearly
all of it is drawing and sound only: the game, its damage and its demos are
unchanged unless a note says otherwise.

## A new episode

**Episode 0.5: SCP_7179_B.** A new entry in the episode menu when you play
DOOM II, TNT or Plutonia. That is all we are going to say about it.

## Climate

**Pick the weather, the time of day, the temperature and the wind.**
F4 → Game → Mode → Weather. Each one is the map's own or a single choice for
every map:

- **Weather:** Clear, Rain, Snow, Nukage rain, Sand, Ash, Fog or Dry ice.
- **Time of day:** Dawn, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Dusk or Night.
- **Temperature:** -30 °C to 50 °C.
- **Wind:** Still, Breeze, Strong or Gale, from any of eight directions.

The menu never offers a combination that doesn't fit: no snow at 40 °C, no
sandstorm in still air, no fog in a gale, no 50 °C at night. Choices follow
the menu's order, so the weather is always all there and a clash moves the
choices below it to the nearest one that fits. Real heat bleaches the sky,
raises a warm haze and shimmers the far ground.

**Snow.** Flakes a pixel wide drift under the sky and blow in through broken
windows. The ground lies white in ragged drifts, deeper the harder it falls,
scoured into long streaks and deep drifts in a gale. Windows frost from
their edges in. Out in the snow the echoes fade and dull.

**Blizzards.** Hard snow in a hard wind turns into a blizzard: flakes
streaking edge to edge, thicker far sheets, and a whiteout that swallows
everything within a few hundred units. Open ground lights evenly in it, the
sky pales toward the horizon, and the whiteout eases in and out at doorways.

**Sand and ash.** Sandstorms with a dust haze, grains that skip and roll in
crowds, and ripples creeping downwind. Ash is volcanic: dark grey, with
glowing embers. Both pile up indoors where they blow in.

**Fog and dry ice.** Fog lies smooth. Dry ice lies banded and heavy, pours
down steps, fills the low streets and pits, creeps in at windows and doors
and leaves walkways and rooftops clear. A hot thing or a blast boils a hole
into either, and the bank fills back in from the edge.

**Water freezes.** Below freezing, water ices over map cell by map cell,
following the air's temperature in each room and drafts from outside, and
gathers into floes. Steps on it sound like stone; it has its own sounds.

**The wind is heard.** Past a breeze it never lets up: a low roar runs
under the gusts and buffets a few times a second.

## Weather that moves

**Rooms and drafts.** At level load DERP works out which sectors make up a
room, which are openings (doors, windows, recesses) and which are porches.
Air flows through the openings, rooms keep their own temperature, and what
falls outside is carried indoors along the drafts: snow trails, slush,
rime round cold inlets, sand fingering in from a doorway.

**The air pushes what flies.** Gusts roll across open ground and shove every
flake, drop and grain. Indoors a draft's jet stirs what rides it, tight at
the opening, swirling where it turns.

**Things disturb the weather.** Rockets, barrels and BFG balls shove what
flies, blow the indoor drifts into a ragged rim, punch holes into fog and
throw up a puff of whatever lay there. Projectiles leave wakes, bodies land
in puffs, footsteps leave prints, bullets kick the floor, slamming doors
breathe out. Torches and anything burning are hot spots: snow melts round
them and the fog boils away.

**The ground keeps the dents.** Outdoors, craters and prints stay in the
snow, sand and ash and fill back in as more falls or the wind blows.

**Blown in.** What comes through a broken window keeps flying the way it
flew outside, then slows indoors. Doorways opened during play lay snow and
rain in front of them as broken windows do. Powder snow settles loosely
and drifts on in the gusts.

**Clear costs nothing.** With Clear weather the drafts, rooms and ground work
are all skipped; the wind is only heard.

## Light

**One light rule.** Sun and sky light now follow a single rule on how much
of the sky each surface really sees, blended across the seams, so nothing
steps where a roof ends. Holes in a roof shade at the room's level, and
sunbeams rise from the whole sun patch, porches included.

**The flashlight lights the weather.** Flakes, drops and grains in the beam
light up, the cone shows in snow, sand and ash, fog and dry ice glow where
it passes, and lying snow and sand glitter.

**Soft shot shadows.** Muzzle flashes, projectiles and burning barrels cast
shadows whose edges step with the artwork and soften like the baked ones.
F4 → Graphics → Lighting → Flashlight and shadows, on by default.

**Metal shading.** Bare metal takes highlights in its own colour, and
mostly blank plates get a brushed sheen running the way the artwork's
streaks do. F4 → Graphics → Surface detail.

**Faster lights and bakes.** Worst views on E1M1 and E1M2 are 1.1 to 1.85 ms
faster on the GPU; bakes and door re-bakes are faster on the CPU.

## Sound

**Tunnel acoustics.** Long narrow passages ring like sewers: a longer tail,
flutter between the side walls (more over water), and no echo coming back
off the far end. Rooms that are no tube sound exactly as before, minus a
small click on big reverb changes that is gone everywhere.

## Phobos

**Physically accurate Phobos is in the main build.** The v0.7.4-phobos
experiment, DOOM's first episode on a moon 22 km across, in vacuum, with
gravity at 1/1700 g, now comes with every download. Pick **Phobos** for
**Gameplay** in F4 → Game → Mode; its options are on F4 → Game → Phobos.
Off by default, never in demos or netgames. New since the experiment:

- **Grav boots:** walk on floors and ceilings; the view rolls over onto the
  ceiling as you pass the middle of the room.
- **The sky is no lid:** you and your rockets go up until about 900 m.
- **F4 → Game → Mode → Gameplay** is one choice, Normal / Authored / Phobos,
  so the authored looks and Phobos never mix.

## Game and controls

**Normal plus movement.** F4 → Game → Controls → Movement is now Normal,
Normal plus or Classic. Normal plus keeps the tight starts and normalized
diagonals, but a running diagonal held for a moment builds up to DOOM's full
strafe-running. Demos and netgames stay classic.

**Missiles fly down the crosshair.** With free aim, your rockets and plasma
leave from the eye and fly along the view's pitch, as bullets do.

**Enemy-appropriate blood.** Cacodemons bleed blue, Barons of Hell and Hell
Knights green, Lost Souls not at all, everyone else red. Splats, spray,
pools and wound rims follow. F4 → Graphics → Combat → Blood.

**"Picked up a mag."** The pistol's ammo pickup no longer claims a clip.
DeHackEd patches still win.

**Ragdolls fly further.** A body thrown far picks up the walls and floors
round where it flies instead of dropping dead at the edge of what it knew.

## Display

**F4 is grouped.** Game, Graphics and Sound sit above the tabs; Tab steps
through every page and PgUp/PgDn switch groups.

**Show FPS.** F4 → Graphics → Display: Off, In the window title, FPS, or
Full, with a frame-time graph, where the time goes, and the systems at work.
The key left of 1 cycles it. Handy for screenshots in bug reports.

**Frame presentation.** VSync, VSync with 3 frames, Fast, Adaptive or Off,
with a frame limit for the uncapped ones.

**Window size.** Set the window to exactly 1280x720 up to 3840x2160, for
recordings and screenshots at a known size. Free is the default.

**Skip hidden walls and floors.** A new Performance switch (off by default)
leaves out geometry hidden behind solid walls and closed doors.

**Smoother over long sessions.** The drawing clock no longer loses precision
after days of play, so fog, weather and water stop stuttering in very long
sessions.

## Downloads and maps

**Play DERP everywhere.** On Windows the program is now **Play DERP.exe**
with the DERP icon; on Linux it is **play-derp** with its own window icon.

**DERPINFO.** Mappers can set a map's climate, sky, sun, fog and more with
a DERPINFO lump. See DERPINFO.md.

**Sky fix for every map.** Sky sectors joined by an open line share the
highest sky, as vanilla shows them: E1M1's south yard no longer slices its
walls off.
